access_notes: VERIFIED 2026-09-04 for T-0507: fetched from the Internet Archive item (HTTP 200, 4013 bytes, matching chicago/reference/ipums/ipums-nhgis.yaml), read, quoted and deleted from the runner. Two checks were made on it before quoting. Its 49 Illinois county totals sum to 157,445, which is the published 1830 total for the state — so the table is the whole state and not a subset. And PEORIA HAS NO ROW, though Peoria County had existed since 1825: the district the Chicago settlement was enumerated in is headed, in the enumerator's hand, 'Peoria & Putnam Counties & Territory attached' (source census_1830_peoria_county_chicago_precinct), and NHGIS prints its total under Putnam. Whether NHGIS merged the two counties or the return itself was credited to Putnam is NOT settled here and must not be asserted from this record.
what_it_supplies: the published 1830 population of the county the Chicago settlement was counted in — 1,310 for Putnam — which is the earliest aggregate this project can place beside the 1835 town census and the 1840 city
the 1830 Illinois state total, 157,445, as a check that the table is complete
what_it_does_not_supply: a population for Chicago. There was no Chicago to count in 1830 and the schedule never writes the word; this is a district of northern Illinois, most of it nowhere near the river
any name, household or age band. It is a county total and nothing else — the names on the same schedule are read from the manuscript at data/research/census_1830/
a growth rate. The 1830 district, the 1835 town and the 1840 city count three different things, and the arithmetic between them in composition_1840.json says so in its own note
note: Quoted, not carried. One number from this table is in the repository, in tools/census_1840_composition.py, where the reasoning that uses it can be read beside it.

transcribes.work: The published aggregate returns of the Fifth Census of the United States, 1830 — the county population totals for Illinois as printed for Congress
transcribes.note: THE DOCUMENT THE ONE QUOTED FIGURE RESTS ON: Putnam County, 1,310, and the state total of 157,445 that checks it. NHGIS ds5 is a machine-readable transcription of these printed totals and adds no count of its own. NOT SEEN BY THIS PROJECT in the printing: what was read is the NHGIS table.
